transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I really appreciate your time. Um... well, I hope I'm answering this right, but... I guess I'm here because folks have been saying my talking gets all mixed up. 

It's probably not a huge deal, I don't want to make a fuss out of it, but... like, I'll try to explain something simple about the keys at work, and then... I don't know, then I'm talking about the jail, and then the prayer rug, and then the chess pieces. And people just look at me and tell me they cannot follow what I'm saying at all. It's a little embarrassing, to be honest, because I try really hard to make sense. Am I explaining that okay for you?
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed your mood being unusually high, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual?

Well, I mean... I wouldn't say "unusually" high, exactly. I just have these really good days sometimes, you know? Like, I feel so... so powerful and happy, and I just want to laugh and talk loud with everybody at work. It's just me being friendly, I think. Is that okay to say? 

But, um... I guess... sometimes if I'm feeling that good and someone questions me or gets in my way, I might... well, I might snap at them a little bit. Shout over something small. I don't mean to be a bother or anything, I just get a little worked up. I really try to keep it under control, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answer.
When you have one of these 'really good days' with high energy and elevated mood, how many days in a row does that usually last?

Well... I hope this doesn't sound too bad, but... those good days, they actually last a pretty long time. It's not just a day or two. When I get like that, with all that energy and all those big plans I want to do... and I barely even need to sleep... it just keeps going. 

If I add it all up, you know, over the years? I guess... well, I guess all those times together probably add up to about a year and eight months. I know that sounds like a lot, and I really hope you don't think less of me for it. I try to manage it, I really do. Is that the kind of information you needed?
Outside of these 'really good' high-energy days, during times when your mood feels normal, do you still notice your speech getting jumbled or hard for others to follow?

Well... um, yes, I suppose so. I really hope this doesn't sound too strange, doctor. I don't want you to think I'm completely out of my mind or anything. But... yes, even when my mood is just fine, just normal, regular days... there are still things that happen. 

Like, there have been weeks where I'm not feeling super high, and I'm not feeling down in the dumps either, just calm. But... well, for like two weeks or more during those calm times, I... I still hear him. The man in the air vents at work. And... and I still notice the people in the building, the way they look at each other, I know they're sending signals about me. 

I try to just do my job and sweep the floors and not bother anybody about it. I really do. But it's still there, even when my mood is totally fine. Does that... is that helpful for you to know? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Roughly how long, in total, have you been experiencing these voices and the feeling that people are sending signals about you—counting all the times together, from when it first started until now?

Well... gosh, if I have to add it all up from the very beginning... I really hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying this, but... I guess the voice in the vents and the... the worrying about the signals and people watching me... if you put all those times together, it's probably been about a year and a half. 

I know that sounds like a really long time to be dealing with something like that, but I promise I still get my work done. I don't let it stop me from sweeping or doing my job. I just... I try to keep my head down and be a good worker, you know? I hope that's not too bad of an answer. Is that what you needed to know?

Since these symptoms first began about a year and a half ago, was there a stretch of at least a month where you had no high-energy or low mood episodes at all, but you were still hearing the voice or noticing the signals?

Well... um, let me think about that for a second. I want to make sure I give you the right answer. 

A whole month with no mood stuff, but still having the... the other things? I... I don't think so? Or maybe I just haven't kept track of it that closely. I mean, I try really hard to just focus on my work and not make a fuss, so I might not have noticed if it was exactly a month like that. 

I'm sorry, I hope it's okay that I don't know for sure. I'm really trying my best to remember everything you're asking. Did I mess up by not knowing that one?

Thinking back over that whole year and a half, would you say the voices and feelings of being watched have been happening mostly during the times you also had those high-energy 'good day' episodes, or have they also been present for long stretches when your mood was completely normal?

Well, um... I guess... I guess they mostly happen together. I really hope I'm explaining this right, doctor. I just want to give you the best answer I can. 

When I look back... the times when I was only sleeping a few hours and, you know, feeling really great and making those big plans for how to reorganize the whole building's cleaning schedule... that's also when I heard the voice in the vents the most. And... and that's when I felt really, really sure that the flickering hallway lights were... were sending warnings about me. 

I know that sounds bad, but I still got all the floors swept, I promise! I didn't let it ruin my work. It's just... yes, those things mostly happened during those really high-energy times. Is that... does that make sense? I hope that's what you were asking.

Can you think of a specific stretch of at least two weeks when your mood was completely normal—not high energy, not low—but you were still hearing the voice in the vents or feeling those signals about you?

Well... gosh, let me think real hard about that. I really want to be helpful here. 

Um... yeah, I guess there was a time... maybe a few weeks, actually? It was... it was a while back, and I remember I was feeling pretty okay. Just, you know, normal. I wasn't having one of those days where I felt like I could clean the whole city, and I wasn't feeling down in the dumps either. I was just... doing my job, being a good worker. 

But... oh, I hope you don't think worse of me for saying this... but even though I felt calm, I... I still heard the man talking in the vents. And I still felt really sure that the people in the building were, you know, making those signals about me. It lasted for... yeah, definitely more than two weeks like that. 

I'm sorry if that's a bad thing to admit. I know I said before they mostly happen together, and I didn't mean to lie to you! I just... I had to really think about it to remember that calmer stretch. I hope I didn't confuse you too much. Am I doing okay with these questions?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits disorganized speech (derailment/tangentiality), persistent auditory hallucinations, and delusions of reference/persecution occurring both during and independent of manic mood episodes. Manic episodes (elevated/irritable mood, decreased sleep, grandiosity, increased goal-directed activity) have been prolonged and recurrent, cumulatively meeting mood episode criteria for a substantial portion of the illness course (~1.5-1.8 years). Critically, patient confirms a distinct period of ≥2 weeks with psychotic symptoms (voices, referential delusions) in the absence of any mood episode, satisfying the core requirement for schizoaffective disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features. The concurrence of mood and psychotic symptoms for most of the illness, plus the manic quality of the mood episodes, supports the bipolar subtype (F25.0) over depressive subtype.
